kārum: dike, embankment of a canal or river (written KAR): kāršu “his dike”, ina kārišu “in his dike”
danānum-D: D-stem of danānum “to be strong”: to strengthen, make firm (a dike): dunnunim (infinitive) “to strengthen”, udanninma (preterite, with -ma) “he strengthened, and …”
pītum: opening, breach, gap (in a dike): pītum (written bi-tum), nominative
petûm-N: N-stem of petûm “to open”: to be opened, to break open: ittepti (perfect) “has opened”, ippetû (preterite, with the relative -u) “(which) was opened, broke open”
ugārum: the irrigated farmland of a district, the commons (written A.GÀR): ugāram, ugārim; mārū ugārim (DUMU A.GÀR{meš}) “the sons of the irrigated land”, the farmers of the district
wabālum-Š: Š-stem of wabālum “to carry”: to make carry off, let (water) carry away: uštābil (perfect) “he has let (the water) carry off”
ḫalāqum-D: D-stem of ḫalāqum “to be lost, to perish”: to destroy, cause to be lost: uḫalliqu (preterite, with the relative -u) “(the grain) he destroyed”
bīšum: movable property, goods, possessions: bīšašu “his goods”
atappum: ditch, small irrigation canal: atappašu “his ditch”
šiqītum: irrigation, watering: šiqītim (genitive) “of irrigation”, ana šiqītim “for irrigation”
šammū: plants, grass, vegetation (plural noun): šammī “(of) the plants”
akālum-Š: Š-stem of akālum “to eat”: to feed, let (animals) graze: šūkulim (infinitive) “to feed”, uštākil (perfect) “he has grazed (the sheep on the field)”, ušākilu (preterite, subjunctive -u) “(who) grazed; (the field) he grazed”
magārum: to agree, consent: imtagarma (perfect, with -ma) “has come to an agreement”, said of a settlement made with another party (itti …)
eṣēdum: to harvest, reap: iṣṣid (present) “he shall harvest”
elēnumma: in addition, over and above, besides; used for a surcharge
20: twenty — two corner-wedges; said ešrā (?) (spoken form reconstructed)
ištu: after, since; from; as a conjunction, “after, once”: ištu … īteliānim “after … have come up”
kannum: band, tie, cord (?): kannū gamartim, a signal hung at the city gate when the grazing season is over (sense from context)
gamartum: completion, end, finish: gamartim (genitive), kannū gamartim “the bands of completion” (?)
ḫalālum-N: N-stem of a verb ḫalālum, “to hang” (?): to be hung up: ittaḫlalū (perfect, plural) “have been hung” — the meaning is inferred from the context
naṣārum: to guard, keep watch over, protect: inaṣṣarma (present, with -ma) “he shall guard, and …”
60: sixty — a single vertical wedge (the sexagesimal “one” of the next order); said šūši (?) “sixty”
nakāsum: to cut, cut down: ikkis (preterite) “he cut down”
1/2: one half — a horizontal crossed by a vertical (the sign for ½); said mišil (?) “half (of)”, followed by the thing halved: mišil mana “half a mina”
zaqāpum: to plant (trees), set upright: zaqāpim (infinitive) “to plant”, izqup (preterite) “he planted”
nukaribbum: gardener, orchard-keeper — written NU.{giš}KIRI₆ “man of the orchard”: nukaribbum, nukaribbim (Harper leaves it as NU.kirû; the Akkadian reading is from later study)
4-kam: four — here a count of years, MU 4{kam}, said erbe šanātim “four years” (spoken form reconstructed)
mitḫāriš: equally, in equal parts, on an equal footing
zittum: share, portion (written ḪA.LA): zittašu, zittišu “his share”
nasāqum: to choose, select: inassaqma (present, with -ma) “he shall choose, and …”
nidītum: land left lying, an unplanted patch, part left over (from nadûm “to leave”): nidītam (accusative)
absinnum: furrow; ploughed, seed-ready land (written AB.SÍN): absinnum (Harper abšênu; the reading of the second sign is uncertain)
nadûm-N: N-stem of nadûm “to leave lying”: to lie neglected, lie fallow: innadû (preterite, with the relative -u) “(in which) it lay neglected”
rakābum-D: D-stem of rakābum “to ride, mount”: to pollinate (date palms): rukkubim (infinitive) “to pollinate”; urakkib(ma) (preterite): lā urakkib “he did not pollinate”
šittān: two-thirds: šittīn (oblique case), the larger share in a three-part division
maṭûm-D: D-stem of maṭûm “to be little”: to reduce, diminish: umtaṭṭi (perfect) “he has reduced”

__broaden__.ina: in, from · at (ina ebūrim “at harvest”); out of (ina bilat kirîm “out of the orchard’s yield”)
__broaden__.eqlum: field (written A.ŠÀ): eqelšu “his field” — the fief-land this whole block protects · bound form eqel (eqel itêšu “his neighbour’s field”; eqel ušākilu “the field he grazed”)
__broaden__.-šu: his / him · -šum “to him, for him” (dative): išakkanūšum, innadnušum
__broaden__.enûm: to change, revoke: īteni “he altered”, enêm “altering” · present inni “he shall change”
__broaden__.ana: to, for · with an infinitive, “to, for” (ana kirîm zaqāpim “to plant as an orchard”); “as” (ana kirîm), “into” (ana libbi), “at the rate of” (ana itêšu)
__broaden__.wabālum: to bring, carry: itbalam “he brought”, lū ublam “let me bring” · ublū (preterite, plural, in a ša-clause) “(the water) carried off”
__broaden__.petûm: to open; of land, to bring into cultivation: iptete “he has opened” · preterite ipte, iptēma “he opened”
__broaden__.bēlum: owner, lord: bēl ḫulqim “owner of the lost property” · owner of a field, bēl eqlim; bēl ḫubullim “creditor” · bēl kirîm “owner of the orchard”
__broaden__.balum: without · (ina) balum bēl eqlim “without (the consent of) the owner of the field”
__broaden__.šattum: year: šattam (syllabic, §31) or MU (the year-sign, §30) · šattim (genitive); plural šanātim “years” (ša šanātim “of the years”); MU 4{kam}, said erbe šanātim “four years”
__broaden__.rabûm-D: D-stem of rabûm: to bring up, raise: urabbāšu “she shall raise him” · urabba (present) “he shall raise (the orchard)”
__broaden__.târum-D: D-stem of târum: to give back: turru “taken away/captured”; utarrūšumma “they shall return (it) to him” · utâr (present) “he shall hand back”
__broaden__.nadānum: to give, pay: inaddin, iddinam, iddinušum; nadānim “to give” · iddin “he gave”; ana kaspim nadānum “to sell”: inaddinūma (present, plural) “they shall sell, and …”
__broaden__.kaspum: silver — the code’s money, written KÙ.BABBAR “shining precious-metal” · kaspim: mišil mana kaspim “half a mina of silver”
__broaden__.elûm: to go up; here: to forfeit: ina kaspišu ītelli “he goes up out of his silver” — his money is gone · to come up: īteliānim (perfect, feminine plural, with the ventive -nim) “(the sheep) have come up”
__broaden__.manûm: mina — weight of silver, 60 shekels (about 500 g): 1 mana kaspim · spelled in syllables, ma-na, at §59: mišil mana kaspim “half a mina of silver”
__broaden__.šaqālum: to weigh out (silver = to pay): išqulu · išaqqal (present) “he shall weigh out”
__broaden__.gamārum: to bring to completion; D-stem gummurum — mugammer “who heaps up (to the full)” · to finish: lā igmur(ma) (preterite) “he did not finish”
__broaden__.ezēbum: to leave; Š-stem šūzubum: ušēzib “he deposited (a document)” · īzib (preterite) “he left (over)”
__broaden__.libbum: heart · ana libbi “into”: ana libbi zittišu “into his share”
__broaden__.šakānum: to set, place: išakkanūšumma “they shall set for him (a term), and” · išakkanūšum (present, plural, dative -šum) “they shall place (it) for him”, i.e. count it to him
__broaden__.nadānum-N: N-stem of nadānum: to be given: innaddin “it shall be given”, innaddiššumma “it shall be given to him” · innadnušum (preterite, subjunctive -u, dative -šum) “(which) was given to him”
__broaden__.epēšum: to do, make: epēšim “doing” · to work (land): ippeš(ma) (present): eqlam šipram ippeš “he shall do the work on the field”
__broaden__.adi: up to, times: adi 12-šu “twelvefold” · as a conjunction, “as long as”, with the subjunctive: adi kirâm ṣabtu “as long as he holds the orchard”
__broaden__.ṣabātum: to seize: iṣṣabat, ṣabtu · stative with the subjunctive -u: adi kirâm ṣabtu “as long as he holds the orchard” (with Harper’s kirûm: “as long as the orchard is held”)
__broaden__.biltum: yield, tribute, rent: nāši biltim “bearer of the yield”, the state tenant (spelled bi-il-tim, or carved with the tribute-sign GUN) · the produce of an orchard or field: biltam, bilat kirîm “the orchard’s yield”, bilat eqlim (written GÚN)
__broaden__.mārum: son (DUMU) — here: a minor, not yet able to sell · member of a group: mārū ugārim (DUMU A.GÀR{meš}) “the sons of the irrigated land”, the district’s farmers
__broaden__.šuāti: that, the aforesaid · as the independent pronoun “him”: šuāti u bīšašu “him and his goods”
__broaden__.nadûm: to cast, throw (a charge; a body into the river): iddi, nadû, iddû · also to leave lying (a field): ittadi “he has left (it) lying” · of a flock: ṣēnī ana eqlim iddi “he turned the sheep loose into a field”
__broaden__.ṣēnum: sheep, the flock: ṣēnē over the sheep-sign LU · also written U₈.UDU{ḫi.a} (ewe + sheep + plural marker): ṣēnū, ṣēnī
